content: Chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 16 (CCL16) is a small cytokine that belongs to the CC chemokine family. It is also referred to as Liver-expressed chemokine (LEC) or Monotactin-1 (MTN-1). This chemokine is primarily expressed in the liver, thymus, and spleen. It exhibits chemoattractive properties, specifically attracting monocytes and lymphocytes to sites of activity. The expression of CCL16 in monocytes can be significantly upregulated by interleukin-10 (IL-10), interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), and bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS). The gene encoding CCL16 is located on chromosome 17 in humans, within a genomic cluster that contains other CC chemokine genes. CCL16 exerts its biological effects by binding to specific cell surface chemokine receptors, including CCR1, CCR2, CCR5, and CCR8. Notably, elevated levels of CCL16 have been detected in human blood plasma. This chemokine may play a role in the recruitment and trafficking of eosinophils, as it has been shown to interact with H4 receptors, which are expressed on eosinophils and mast cells. Additionally, CCL16 has been demonstrated to suppress the rapid proliferation of myeloid progenitor cells, suggesting a potential regulatory role in hematopoiesis.
